text:
priya: Heads-up — several support tickets came in around 07:18-07:30 UTC reporting p95/p99 spikes for Dedicated pools in eu-west-1. Customers see token latency jump ~2-3x and some 504s. I posted customer traces in the tickets.
cheng: Seen it on our dashboards too. p95 jumped from ~70ms to ~210ms around 07:20. p99s are into the 800ms-1.2s range.
alex: Any pattern on which pool(s)? model types?
priya: So far mostly ml-dense-8 pools backed by A100s, Dedicated tier. Affected pools: pool-ded-eu-3 and pool-ded-eu-4.
maria: Not seeing infra maintenance in the timeline. No cloud-scale events reported.
support-lead: Customer A on pool-ded-eu-3 opened an escalation. They've got SLA sensitivity. They're seeing sustained degraded tail latency and occasional request failures when autoscaler is triggering.
cheng: I pulled some traces. Looks like scale-up path is issuing instance creation but GPU warmup (nv-init + model load) is taking ~90-120s during these episodes. Autoscaler times out after 60s and retries, which floods the queue.
priya: That matches customer repro: they send a burst, autoscaler tries to add nodes, but requests queue and then time out (504s).
infra-bot: Observed VM lifecycle events: create->startup->attached->online timings spiked at 07:20-07:40. Median attach latency normal but tails hit 2m.
ops-bot: Alert: Dedicated pool pool-ded-eu-3 saturated (85% alloc) and failing to recover within cooldown window.
alex: Can we reproduce quickly in staging? If scale-up path is slow, maybe kernel driver or image pull is slow.
cheng: Repro steps I used: 1) spin up a small Dedicated pool in staging (same config). 2) send ramped burst: 200 concurrent short-generation requests with 1-2 tokens. 3) watch autoscaler metrics + instance events.
cheng: Command I used to simulate:
```
hey load --concurrency 200 --duration 60s --endpoint https://staging.api.redwood.internal/v1/generate --header "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" --body '{"model": "ml-dense-8", "input": "hi"}'
```
priya: Logs show many kube-proxy restarts on the nodes being added? Any kube events?
maria: Checked k8s events for the node bootstrap pods — some image pull backoffs were happening (registry 503 retries). That would delay container startup and model loading.
alex: Huh, registry 503s could be flaky CDN at that time. But why only Dedicated pools? Hosted uses different AMI/registry path.
cheng: Dedicated nodes pull model artifacts from S3 via our init container. If init starts late (image pull + s3 cold read), the runtime isn't ready. Also saw NV driver init taking longer on some instances (kernel messages: `nvidia-modeset: failed to initialize` then success after retries).
support-lead: Customer-facing mitigation needed ASAP. What can we do short-term?
priya: Short-term mitigations: 1) Increase autoscaler timeout from 60s -> 180s for the affected pools so new instances aren't considered failed during slow boot. 2) Temporarily raise min capacity for pools currently under pressure to avoid triggering scale-up. 3) Route traffic to compatible fallback model variants (half-precision) while we stabilize.
alex: I can flip autoscaler timeout to 180s for pool-ded-eu-3/4 via control-plane toggle. Doing it now (will monitor).
ops-bot: Action: set_autoscaler_timeout pool-ded-eu-3 180s by alex at 07:45 UTC.
priya: Also can we enable pre-warming: keep one warm spare instance per pool to avoid cold boot for small bursts? That might raise cost but reduces tail risk.
maria: I scheduled a temporary increase to min_replicas from 2 -> 4 on pool-ded-eu-3. Doing it now.
infra-bot: min_replicas change applied to pool-ded-eu-3 by maria at 07:48 UTC.
cheng: After the autoscaler timeout/op adjustments I re-ran the load test. Observed p95 back to ~90ms, p99s ~280ms. Cold-start 95th improved. No 504s in the test.
priya: Good. We should still root cause registry/S3 delays and NV driver flakiness.
alex: On longer-term fixes: 1) implement async model prefetch to local cache during node spin-up so model load doesn't block readiness. 2) improve node bootstrap retries and metricization so autoscaler uses 'node_got_runtime' instead of just 'node_ready' kernel signal. 3) add a warm-pool knob (config per pool) that keeps a configurable number of pre-initialized workers.
cheng: Also add more robust fallback routing: if Dedicated pool is saturated, fall back to lower-latency hosted instances for critical customers with consent, and throttle non-critical traffic.
support-lead: For customers with escalations: send interim update — we've increased autoscaler timeout and min capacity, and are scheduling deeper infra investigation. Next update in 60m.
priya: I'll draft the message. Key points: cause likely node boot/model-init tail due to registry/S3 & driver init; mitigations applied; long-term engineering tasks created.
oncall: FYI I've captured the incident in incidents/ and created a sev-3 ticket. Link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ENG-INC-2027 (internal).
priya: Repro notes attached for engineers: exact load command above, pool config snapshot, and node bootstrap logs:
```
[2027-07-16T07:21:05Z] node-init: pulling image registry.redwood/internal/runtime:sha-abcdef
[2027-07-16T07:21:38Z] image-pull: 503 Service Unavailable (retry 3)
[2027-07-16T07:22:40Z] s3-get model.tar.gz: 503 slow read (multi-part retries)
[2027-07-16T07:23:10Z] nvidia: modeset init try 2 -> success
[2027-07-16T07:23:28Z] model unpack -> 45s
[2027-07-16T07:24:13Z] runtime ready
```
cheng: I'll instrument a new probe metric node_runtime_ready_ms and add it to the autoscaler policy evaluation. Can do a PR today.
maria: I'll follow-up with infra/registry ops to check CDN health and S3 proxy logs around the window.
alex: For immediate customer relief, I've also enabled a soft-fail fallback route for pool-ded-eu-3: requests that would queue > 2s are routed to hosted low-latency fallback for SLA customers. Will keep this for 2 hours.
support-lead: Customers A/B/C notified. They're appreciative of the quick mitigation. One wants a postmortem.
priya: We'll produce a short postmortem once we have root cause. Action items recap in ticket: 1) infra: investigate registry/S3 tail (maria). 2) runtime: add node_runtime_ready_ms + autoscaler change (cheng). 3) control plane: warm-pool capability + prefetch design (alex). 4) docs: update runbook for Dedicated pool coldstart (priya).
oncall: Oncall handoff at 08:00 UTC to jamal. Jamal - you have the incident.
jamal: Taking it. I'll watch alerts and coordinate with infra.
priya: Thanks all. We'll reconvene if anything regresses. :thumbsup:
